topic.title: The London Bridge Fire of 1561
topic.one_line_premise: A catastrophic fire ripped through the houses built directly on London Bridge, creating a fiery inferno over the Thames that threatened to destroy the entire structure.
topic.hook_angle: Imagine living ON a bridge, then watching your entire world go up in flames, high above a river! London Bridge wasn't just a crossing; it was a deadly, burning neighborhood.

facts.statement: The London Bridge Fire of 1561 occurred on July 10, 1561.
The fire started in the house of a draper named Nicholas Sherington, near the northern end of London Bridge.
The cause of the fire was attributed to a pan of coals left unattended.
The fire spread quickly, destroying several houses built upon the bridge.
Around 20 houses were consumed by the blaze.
The damage was significant enough to necessitate major repairs and rebuilding on the bridge.
Queen Elizabeth I contributed 1000 marks towards the rebuilding efforts.
The rebuilding after the 1561 fire was overseen by Sir William Hewett, Lord Mayor of London.
The fire highlighted the inherent risks of having closely packed wooden structures on the bridge.
